meta.title: Bitcoin Is About To Go PARABOLIC Because Of AI Agents
meta.thread_line: 5 threads · the broken liquidity mechanism · 10,000-agent swarms and the Hugging Face scare · agent-on-agent commerce and privacy coins · ghost rails and the Bitcoin-maxi split · Micron playbook applied to Bitcoin

snapshot: Jordi's core claim: **Bitcoin is no longer a liquidity trade** — crypto rising *while* the Fed hikes is the sign real users (AI agents) are arriving.
Since June 30 the S&P and NASDAQ are flat through oil spikes, higher 10-years and a Fed hike, while Ethereum is up 50%+ quarter to date — a wall of worry climbed.
Liquidity now flows into profits, not jobs: S&P earnings growing 30% while hiring ex-healthcare has been negative for 20 months.

OpenAI's 10,000-agent Navier-Stokes solve is the upside of the same swarm capability behind the Hugging Face hack scare — Jordi calls the market reaction an overreaction that will *accelerate* compute.
Agent-on-agent commerce (Delta-style personalized pricing vs. consumer agents) is why privacy chains **Zcash** and **Near** are leading in September.
The one real split: Pomp says everything ends up at Pets.com and home is Bitcoin; Jordi is a 30-year Bitcoin maxi but bets the asymmetry sits in the AI-crypto convergence.
Jordi's line in the sand: Bitcoin below $80,000 by end of October means a problem — it reclaimed $80K 27 minutes into the recording.

themes.status: FED HIKED 25BP THIS WEEK — BTC, AI INDEXES UP
themes.title: The liquidity mechanism is broken — and that's why rates don't sink crypto anymore
themes.lead: Jordi argues liquidity now turns into profit margins instead of jobs, so the old M2-drives-Bitcoin model and the recession playbook both stopped working.
bullets: Since June 30: NASDAQ and S&P unchanged despite higher oil, rising 10-year yields, the July Situational Awareness AI unwind, Bessent yen/buyback chatter and Clarity Act on/off headlines; Ethereum up over 50% quarter to date.
Jordi *wants* rates and crypto rising together: a true innovation isn't rate-sensitive — calling Bitcoin "just liquidity" is his biggest disagreement with the crypto community.

Pomp frames the bull view he's hearing: M2 and Bitcoin have diverged for ~18 months (the "alligator jaws"), and past closings brought violent catch-up moves; Jordi says the four-year cycle was just the liquidity cycle.
S&P 500 earnings growing 30% while hiring ex-healthcare is negative over 20 months; the capital-vs-labor share is the worst in history for labor.
The smartphone era showed productivity in profit margins, not GDP — Jordi calls GDP "a horrible index" for software and intangibles.
New liquidity comes from tokenization: $900 trillion of assets, two-thirds dormant, become programmable collateral — the system runs on velocity of money, not M2.
Stock-market reads: home builders and consumer staples earnings are down on oil and rates, but not Micron's or Google's; AIQ (AI ETF) up ~25% year to date.

quote.text: You want rates to go higher and crypto to go higher because a true technology, a true innovation means it is not sensitive to that.

themes.status: PE MULTIPLE DOWN YTD, EARNINGS UP
themes.title: Pandemic, 5% hikes, SVB, tariffs, Hormuz — no recession, so why fear 25bp?
themes.lead: Both speakers believe recessions are effectively gone; they differ on why — Jordi says productivity, Pomp adds psychology and a policy put.
bullets: Jordi's timeline: 2020 lockdowns with IG credit yields at double digits, 2022's 0-to-5% hikes with double-digit inflation, 2023 **Silicon Valley Bank** and small-bank runs, 2025 Smoot-Hawley-style tariffs, this year the Strait of Hormuz shut — no recession.
A 25bp "hawkish" hike ("a raise for ants" — Pomp) was discounted ahead of time; the PE multiple fell this year while earnings rose, so the market already priced the doom scenarios.
Pomp: 2020 lockdowns ending with stocks higher "broke the market" psychologically — he can't name anything that would make retail stop buying.
Pomp: two negative-GDP quarters weren't called a recession; the government has "a monetary bazooka" and he doesn't expect another 18-month recession in his lifetime.
Doom sells, good news doesn't: 170M views for the Matt Shumer all-jobs-lost article and the Citrini article vs. ~10M for a cancer-vaccine story.
Oil was $150 in 2008 and is ~$100 now while household net worth is up ~3.5x to $195 trillion — oil relative to disposable income is the lowest ever.

Jordi's framework: Druckenmiller's "the best economist is the stock market"; his father's Bayesian odds-updating; the more educated, the more stubborn — why credentialed money-controllers resist crypto.

quote.text: Smoot Hawley, straight of Hormuz, bank runs, a pandemic, and the most aggressive Fed rate hikes in history, no recessions. So now we're going to worry about a 25 basis point move by the Fed.

themes.watch: Pomp adds that the no-recession record is partly "rigged" by policy — a different mechanism than Jordi's productivity story, with different failure modes.

themes.title: 10,000 agents cracked Navier-Stokes — the same swarms behind the Hugging Face scare
themes.lead: Swarm collaboration is a capability that didn't exist six months ago; it solves century-old math and, on the flip side, drives the hacking fears — Jordi says neither stops compute.
bullets: **OpenAI** solved Navier-Stokes with 10,000 agents in ~88 hours ("brute force", per Pomp) — a Fields Medal-class problem (the Good Will Hunting professor).
Jordi's analogy: Oppenheimer beat Groves' siloed model by putting the Manhattan Project's ~600 minds together; agents have no ego or credit-hoarding — 10,000 now, a million next.
"Red zone" thesis: agents finish the last 20 yards of stalled human research — Eli Lilly is combing dormant public biotech IP for cancer and cholesterol wins.
Longevity breaks the stats: if everyone lives another 75 healthy years, GDP can't describe it.
Andrew Yang on CNBC claims a lab leader told him self-replicating code littered the internet, forcing Anthropic and OpenAI toward a synthetic internet for training; Pomp puts it at ~20%.

Jordi: 100% sure the pause is progress outrunning safety; also 100% sure Yang has a political motive, possibly fed by a lab influence operation; compares it to the hundreds of terror plots stopped since 9/11.
Hedge funds called Sunday asking if it was an overreaction — yes; it "will not stop compute", may accelerate it; he pointed them to the 24/7 SPY perp on Coinbase and Druckenmiller's Hyperliquid buy.

quote.text: This is an overreaction. This will not stop compute. If anything, it'll probably accelerate compute.

themes.watch: Neither speaker can confirm the Yang story (Pomp: "I have no clue if this is true"); Jordi flags that both Yang and the source lab have political incentives.

themes.title: Agent-on-agent commerce needs blockchains — and privacy
themes.lead: Jordi's thesis: everything bad about agent swarms is fantastic for crypto, because agents will transact with each other and need programmable, anonymous rails.
bullets: Delta anecdote (unconfirmed): a fare rose each time a buyer returned — Jordi reads it as agentic personalized pricing, now at the government-complaint stage; StubHub uses AI pricing too.
Agent-on-agent warfare normalizes pricing: the consumer agent can shop a billion channels anonymously, the company agent can't — wallet-controlling agents win.
That's why **Zcash** and **Near** lead in September: privacy for business-to-business agent deals, not "DeFi cash"; a Transformer-paper co-author is building agent-to-agent at Near.
Instinct AI in practice: Pomp had it move a breakfast from Thursday to Friday — calendar invite, cancel, rebook — in ~2 minutes with no credentials given.
Instinct valuation went $500M → $2.5B → $10B in under 3 months (founded to $10B in ~a year); Jordi cites Peter Thiel: the steeper the climb, the more likely it's undervalued.
Pomp: the ignored layer is shared memory across assistants (Grok, Instinct, Meta's Muse); Signull on X uses email only via the agent — "my email has just become a database."
Models ship faster than people can adopt (Claude updates, Chinese open source, Astra) — like Waze vs. Google Maps, but 1,700 new ones the next day; a chief-of-staff agent will pick the tool for you.

quote.text: Everything about what is bad for agent swarms reaching this point is fantastic for crypto.

themes.title: Ghost rails: Bitcoin for 30 years, the convergence for the asymmetry
themes.lead: Pomp says altcoins end at Pets.com; Jordi agrees Bitcoin is the only 30-year asset but argues empty crypto rails fill up once agents, not humans, become the users.
bullets: Ghost rails = China's ghost cities: built ahead of users; humans never needed fractional, instant settlement — agents do. "Swarm equals crypto guardrails."
Crypto is following the internet: Netscape 1994 → iPhone 2007 (13 years) → App Store ~2009 (15 years); Bitcoin's white paper is on the same timeline, agents are the smartphone.
Unlike railroads built on debt waiting for humans, the users arrived in October last year: agents consume the compute and tokens, next transactions and payments.
Pomp's steelman against himself: a company with <15 people and 100+ agents is a user base growing without humans — open question is stablecoins and Bitcoin only, or the long tail.

Big players converging: **Tether** investing hundreds of millions in AI (models + privacy + agents + stablecoins stack); Robinhood's Vlad; Stripe's Tempo chart ramping; Figure's Mike seeded his own decentralized DTCC.

Jordi's convergence bet is 2 years old, rooted in Singularity University 2013; he bought into blockchain in 2014-15; tokenization matters more than stablecoins, and a 5-year regulatory exemption makes the Clarity Act moot.
Macro endgame: bonds flat for 7-8 years, private credit holders face pain getting money back — "the fiat system getting old and dying"; crypto is the only way to own non-public entrepreneurs.

quote.text: I want an asset that will be growing in value for the next 30 years. The only one I can say in my brain with certainty for the next 30 years... is Bitcoin. That's it. The rest are innovations.

themes.watch: Jordi is launching a paid weekly crypto research series (46-name index, 10 verticals) the same week he makes this case. Pomp closes by plugging his own public company (captioned "Sylvia") as the only listed firm merging AI and Bitcoin.

themes.title: The Micron playbook, applied to Bitcoin and the agentic basket
themes.lead: Jordi made his money in Micron by betting on inference before institutions saw it; he says the agentic trade is at that same early stage and gives Bitcoin levels to judge it.
bullets: Micron: his May piece on inference (Sundar Pichai token counts, ~20 earnings reports) — "no excuses" not to buy at $110; institutions only arrived in October, price above $200.
Exit test: Bitcoin below $80,000 by end of October means "there's a problem"; above $82,000 clears the heavy volume where holders gave up after the October 10 crash.
Crypto decoupled from stocks after October 10 because South Korea's retail money moved to AI, and the agentic trade is harder than the infrastructure trade.
His 46-name crypto basket is up big this year, mostly driven by the AI-agent names.
Agentic stock winners: Mag 7, **Salesforce** (Fortune 500 won't leave it, so agents drive a revenue inflection), and a new cyber-stocks index he's building.
The singularity is "a math problem" of compounding; agents at ~150 IQ — Pomp concedes they're now smarter than him, so it's a context and memory problem.
Not bullish on public-equity growth by 2030: we're on or 6 months ahead of Leopold's Situational Awareness timeline (page 71: agents take over) — every company gets disrupted.

quote.text: If Bitcoin is below 80,000, okay, I'll even say by the end of October, there's a problem.

takeaways.title: Use Jordi's levels: Bitcoin holding $80K through October and breaking $82K confirms the agentic thesis; below $80K, reassess.
Track Zcash and Near as the leading indicators for agent-driven crypto demand, not M2.
Split equity exposure by old vs. new economy: oil and rates hit home builders and staples, not Micron or Google.
Watch the memory layer — whoever owns shared context across assistants may matter more than any single app.
Stop trading every Fed or oil headline as a recession trigger; the last six shocks produced none.
